Exceptions inside the dispatch try become status=unavailable with ex.ToString, preserving actual errors rather than substituting output. Discovery before the try and the final file write can still throw. The full error string is suitable for private experiment output, not assumed path-free publication.

blocks.title: Synthesize references to raw PCM without a playback destination
blocks.explanation: Input JSON is a list of job dictionaries. One synthesizer at rate zero selects each job's installed voice, writes to a fresh MemoryStream in the fixed format, speaks the text, detaches output and writes raw PCM bytes to the named path. Nested using blocks dispose streams and synthesis state. The result records the job count. Paths and field types are trusted harness inputs; this helper does not create destination parents or validate jobs as a public service would.

blocks.title: Translate callback-driven recognition into one file result
blocks.explanation: Decode owns a read-only MemoryStream over WAV bytes and an AutoResetEvent. SpeechRecognized appends only nonblank recognized text; RecognizeCompleted captures the engine error and signals completion. Both handlers are attached before starting recognition in the next block, so completion cannot race past an unattached listener. The returned sentence is composed from recognized events, not an arbitrary final partial. External System.Speech callback ordering and native behavior remain library boundaries.

blocks.title: Bound asynchronous dictation and detach all event handlers
blocks.explanation: The engine reads the provided WAV stream and runs RecognizeMode.Multiple. A 60-second timeout triggers cancellation and up to five seconds for its completion signal, then throws even if cancellation completes. A callback-reported error is rethrown. Finally always unsubscribes handlers and clears input, avoiding accumulation across repeated Decode calls; using then disposes the event and stream. Joined parts are returned only after successful completion. There is no microphone input or speaker output in this function.

blocks.title: Load installed dictation and disclose adaptation uncertainty
blocks.explanation: Recognize selects the first installed en-US recognizer and records unavailable rather than installing one when absent. Cases and WAV bytes are loaded before the cold-load stopwatch. Engine construction, dictation grammar, silence/babble limits and attempted AdaptationOn=0 are inside load timing. The end-silence thresholds are 500 ms; initial silence is five seconds and babble fifteen. Failure to disable adaptation is recorded as a string and does not fail the run, so this path cannot promise adaptation was always off.

blocks.title: Warm once, then time complete file decodes
blocks.explanation: The first case is decoded once as a separately timed warmup, not a scored repeat row. Nested repeat/case loops time the complete Decode call with Stopwatch and save ID, repeat index, actual recognized text and elapsed seconds. The parent bench.run adds common WER afterward. Engine disposal is scoped by using and successful completion sets status=ok. This bridge assumes a nonempty case list and valid repeats supplied by the harness; direct callers do not receive the Python manifest validation automatically.

files.role: Specify local-output, WAV-format and corpus-identity guards using mocks instead of real audio or models.

blocks.title: Reject obvious output escapes and accept a private child path
blocks.explanation: The test imports bench, then calls only its path helper. It expects ValueError for a repository-root output and a LOCAL/../ escape, while a LOCAL child returns the resolved intended path. This tests lexical/resolved containment without writing files. It does not demonstrate ACL privacy, encryption, concurrent path-swap safety or enforcement by every quality helper; bench's import-time environment assignments still occur.

blocks.title: Use a near-valid WAV mock to reject 44.1 kHz input
blocks.explanation: A mocked wave context reports mono, two-byte uncompressed samples but 44100 Hz. pcm_from_wav must raise rather than resampling, isolating sample rate as the changed field. The path is unused and no audio device/file decode runs. This single case does not independently cover stereo, compressed data, wrong sample width or malformed WAV headers, even though production code checks their format tuple.

blocks.title: Reject duplicate IDs and empty corpora before inference
blocks.explanation: Two dictionaries deliberately share an ID while using different filenames/references. read, pcm_from_wav and sha are mocked, and the expected Duplicate ValueError proves identity validation rather than file availability. A separate mocked empty list must fail. These are guard tests, not model accuracy or waveform integrity tests; the module guard runs unittest only on explicit execution.

files.role: Lock common normalization, edit counts and word-weighted aggregation semantics with small deterministic examples.

blocks.title: Keep punctuation, numbers and apostrophes engine-neutral
blocks.explanation: Tests require case/punctuation variants to score zero, digits including time/decimal/percent to normalize like their English spoken forms, grouped 1,000 to match one thousand, and ASCII/curly apostrophes to produce dont. Assertions compare normalized values rather than accepting an engine-specific rewrite. They cover selected English examples, not all num2words formats, Unicode scripts or malformed numeric punctuation.

blocks.title: Retain each edit type and undefined empty-reference rates
blocks.explanation: Single substitution, deletion and insertion examples isolate their counters. An empty hypothesis deletes all three reference words. An empty reference retains a hello insertion but has None WER instead of a division error. cat versus dog horse bird asserts WER=3, preserving insertions rather than clamping accuracy to a percentage range. These tests constrain numeric semantics, not the quality of any ASR engine.

blocks.title: Prevent averaging case percentages and check a mixed alignment
blocks.explanation: One wrong one-word case plus a correct four-word case must aggregate to one error over five words, WER 0.2. The assertion explicitly rules out an unweighted average of per-case WER. A mixed cat/dog and omitted/added-word example requires three edits. That example checks total distance, not all possible tie decompositions; deterministic tie policy is read from metrics.errors itself. The final guard invokes unittest only on direct execution.

files.role: Guard the secondary character metric against special-case reference repair and hidden hallucination/repetition errors.

blocks.title: Show generic whitespace tolerance with real-error negative controls
blocks.explanation: leet code/LeetCode and any compound/AnyCompound both require zero character edits, demonstrating a generic join-normalized-words rule rather than a LeetCode-only exception. lead code and to some must still produce errors against leet code and two sum. The tests exercise pure scoring functions, not a recognizer; importing quality_receipt also imports helper modules and their environment setup but does not enter their main functions.

blocks.title: Retain hallucinations and all character edit operations
blocks.explanation: An empty reference with hallucination must retain thirteen inserted characters while the rate is None. abc/ac, abc/adc and abc/abxc require one deletion, substitution and insertion respectively through the common distance implementation. These examples ensure whitespace removal does not erase genuine spelling changes; they do not validate public receipt field allowlists or cross-engine input equality.

blocks.title: Count repeated phrases rather than deduplicating model output
blocks.explanation: Repeating tea or coffee twice against one reference occurrence must add three word insertions and nonzero character distance. This guards against a superficially flattering deduplication step that would hide model repetition. The file then closes with a normal unittest entry guard. No test is claimed to have run during this documentation task, and these cases do not qualify timing, audio devices or live providers.
